summary: Tenant prefetch induced kernel-fallback causing API gateway 502s and streaming interrupts on private eu-west cluster
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12T08:15Z Acme Health reported elevated 5xx rates on requests routed to their private eu-west deployment. Symptoms included repeated 502/503 responses from the API gateway for short requests and frequent streaming session disconnects for long-running chat sessions. Impact: Several customer endpoints returned transient failures (~8-25% error rate for affected routes) and streaming sessions for a subset of users dropped mid-response. Environment: Private deployment in eu-west (customer-controlled VPC with Redwood Private runtime). Time window: 2026-03-12T08:10Z to ongoing. This ticket captures initial triage, mitigations applied, and next steps for a permanent fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send mixed small text-generation and streaming chat traffic to the customer's pinned route at ~100r/s using their API key
2) Observe transient 502/503 responses from api-gateway logs and short-lived streaming disconnects in stream sessions
3) Correlate with serving-runtime metrics: increased kv-prefetch stall rate, elevated kernel-fallback events, and GPU memory eviction logs
4) Reproduce in staging by replaying a subset of Acme Health production trace (see related_confluence_pages)
logs: [2026-03-12T08:12:03Z] apigw: upstream 502 from runtime-rt-03 (conn reset) route=/v1/chat stream_id=abc123
[2026-03-12T08:12:04Z] runtime-rt-03: PREFETCH lock wait=1290ms tenant=acme-health model=gpt-neo-2.7B-quant
[2026-03-12T08:12:05Z] kernel: nvml: GPU0 memory eviction triggered by OOM reserve; pid=4271
[2026-03-12T08:12:06Z] apigw: streaming session tear-down reason=upstream-unavailable stream_id=abc123
investigation_notes: 08:15 - Support acknowledged customer report and opened this ticket. Initial dashboards show apigw 502 spikes correlating with runtime kernel-fallback metrics.
08:22 - SRE (Lina Chen) checked node-level metrics: GPU memory usage increased on a small set of dedicated pods; nvml evictions correlated with prefetch activity from the tenant.

08:35 - Hypothesis: aggressive prefetch for quantized model variant (q8_0) triggers a kernel selection path that falls back to fp32 kernels on certain GPUs; fallback increases memory working set and causes eviction/ooms under mixed small/streaming load.
08:50 - Reproduced locally in staging by replaying a 30s trace with mixed small requests + streaming keepalive; observed identical kernel-fallback traces and OOMs when q8_0 patch applied.
09:10 - Observed api-gateway retry amplification for short requests: hedged retries + upstream restart loops amplified error rates; apigw hit thread/conn limits temporarily.
09:30 - Confirmed customer was using a pinned model variant with quant config enabled in their Private config - this variant differs from hosted defaults.

Actions taken: (a) Temporarily reduced Acme Health prefetch concurrency (rate limiting at 60% of baseline) via route-level config; (b) disabled the q8_0 quant fallback flag on their runtime nodes by toggling kernel-selection guard; (c) applied transient autoscale of +2 GPU workers to the private pool to absorb load.
Preliminary outcome: after mitigations 09:50Z, 502 rate dropped from 18% -> 3% and streaming disconnects fell to background levels. Monitoring remains under watch.

Open questions: whether kernel-selection logic should avoid fp32 fallback for q8_0 (prefer failing fast to avoid OOM) or whether automatic eviction thresholds need tuning for mixed workloads. Also need to evaluate prefetch heuristics for private deployments with limited GPU headroom.

2026-03-12T08:25Z - Lina Chen (SRE): Confirmed GPU nvml evictions on runtime-rt-03/04 and high kv-prefetch lock wait times. Noted kernel_fallback events in runtime logs.

2026-03-12T09:05Z - Aarti Kumar (Acme Health): We saw large numbers of short request failures starting 08:10Z; several users reported chat sessions dropping. Appreciate quick mitigation — please advise on ETA for a permanent fix.

2026-03-12T09:40Z - Diego Ramos (Eng): Applied temporary kernel-selection guard and prefetch throttle to customer's nodes; autoscaled +2 workers. Need engineering follow-up to add guard into runtime to fail fast on unsupported quant kernels.

2026-03-13T11:00Z - Omar Haddad (Runtime Eng): Created draft PR to add a configurable kernel selection policy and a safety threshold to avoid fallback that increases memory footprint. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894

resolution: Mitigations applied: (1) rate-limited tenant prefetch concurrency at route level (temporary), (2) toggled kernel-fallback guard to prevent memory-expanding fallbacks for q8_0, (3) added +2 GPUs to private pool to absorb current load. Short-term status: error rate reduced to ~2-4% on affected routes and streaming disconnects largely resolved. Permanent work: implement runtime kernel-selection policy change (PR #2894) to prefer failing fast on unsupported quant kernels or select low-memory fallback paths; add unit/integration tests for mixed prefetch + streaming load; update prefetch heuristics for private/pinned deployments; tune apigw retry hedging to avoid amplification. Postmortem and customer-facing RCA to be delivered by 2026-03-19. Follow-ups tracked in linked INT issue INT-4012 and runtime PR.
